gen-gf-warnes-gf-chivo: Chivo reads as a plain sans with its lowercase packed tight under the caps and daylight showing through every curve. Warnes earns its place big and brief, where its stretched, monoline strokes can spread out.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-chocolate-classical-san: Warnes draws its ink strokes tapering off before they touch, with no tilt to the round letters. Chocolate Classical Sans has a sizable lowercase and a broad-nibbed stroke, so shrinking the heading would waste that bold, stretched spacing.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-comme: Comme reads smooth, with no clogged curves anywhere in its lowercase. Warnes sets a stretched, ballpoint-like line above it, and the sans-serif text below fills most of each letter's height with quiet, modern ease.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-cossette-texte: Loud, stretched ink up top, then a wide-eyed text face. Cossette Texte keeps a prominent x-height and sturdy n arches, which gives the expressive Warnes a sans-serif partner that holds its ground.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-duru-sans: Warnes looks bold and spacious, its curves never thinning at the shoulders. Duru Sans follows with wide openings and big lowercase bodies, so a longer passage would feel open and modern, with ascenders barely announcing themselves.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-fresca: Expressive is the right word for Warnes, with its tapered ink strokes and stretched spacing. And Fresca keeps its counters connected to outside space under short ascenders, so a longer passage would read cleanly, with no calligraphic thinning.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-funnel-sans: Expressive, spacious Warnes sets the tone with ink strokes that taper before they touch. Funnel Sans brings a steady, professional stroke and a pried-open e, making the sans-serif text feel like firm ground under it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-gafata: Warnes leads with a single-weight outline feel, its stretched ink strokes tapering off before they touch. And Gafata, a contemporary sans-serif, holds a tall band of letters with short stalks, so a longer stretch reads steadily.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-geist: Warnes stands out for ink strokes that taper before touching, with no thick and thin at all. Geist, a quiet sans with wide-open shapes and solid word blocks, would swallow a heading made small.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-georama: Georama reads approachable, with a wide-open c like a bracelet pulled apart and barely rising capitals. Georama keeps a longer passage easygoing, while Warnes above it stays monoline, stretched and expressive.
